description: Use when deciding when to commit repository work, including ideation, brainstorming, planning, implementation, verification, fixes and documentation.

# Commit completed results

Use compound-engineering:ce-commit for every local commit.

Commit completed tasks or substantive independently useful, verified substages.
Labels, task entry, answers, turns, small edits and passing checks alone are
not boundaries. Accumulate related changes. Save documents/decisions/memory
promptly without committing every save. Short tasks usually need one final
commit; long work may preserve independent completed results. Set no
question/file/line/time thresholds.

Exceptions: explicit commit-now instruction or justified checkpoint before
concrete risk. Explain command/risk; preserve workflow gates, isolation and recovery.
Group related steps before dispatch; never bypass a safety transaction.

Before committing read [work safety](references/work-safety.md) and
[message transfer](references/message-transfer.md), then apply
harness/common/skills/comm-check-publication-data/SKILL.md.
Run appropriate checks. Inspect current ownership; the orchestrator commits
only authorized owned changes through explicit file lists, preserving unrelated
work and exclude: paths. No empty/duplicate commits.

Missing Git/ce-commit, failed checks/commit: preserve changes and report.
Done: hash/subject for completed owned results or clean skip. No push, PR,
merge, history rewriting, route choice or verification upgrade is granted.
comm-commit-task-stages.references/message-transfer.md:
# Transfer Git/PR text as data

Use a structured tool/API parameter without constructing shell code. With CLI,
write text safely as file data; use the body's body-file option or git commit -F.
Create the file without executable substitutions. Pass paths and titles safely too.
JSON serialization inserted into a shell string is not shell escaping.
Preserve intended Markdown, quotes and newlines; protect every shell-sensitive
construct, not only backticks. Verify the actually saved title/body/message.
This resource performs no commit and grants no history rewrite or PR action.
comm-commit-task-stages.references/work-safety.md:
# Before a Git mutation

Identify repository/worktree, branch/HEAD, intended operation and relevant
staged, unstaged and untracked changes; distinguish owned, foreign and unknown.
Preserve foreign edits and their exact staging, including shared files.
Never stash, commit, reset, clean or move unrelated work to make a clean tree.
Checkpoints retain the commit owner's gates.

Do not overlap an unsafe operation with an active writer to affected files,
index or shared refs. Coordinate completion or authorized isolation; never
stop another writer automatically. Worktrees are optional and share some refs/config.
Unknown ownership or unsafe overlap blocks dependent mutation: explain and wait;
independent reads may continue. Inspect again when relevant state changes.
